title: Note titles and shared-note titles are written into innerHTML unescaped (stored XSS, also from the server)
evidence: Driven in Chromium. Seeded localStorage with title '': window.__xss === 1 after load. Mocked /api/shared to return the same markup as a shared title: window.__xss2 === 1 after typing in the search box. Sinks: app.js:10-12 (n.title through a template string into list.innerHTML) and app.js:46 (s.title through insertAdjacentHTML).
failing_case: Another user shares a note titled . Any visitor who types in the search box runs it and leaks every note in localStorage. A user who pastes such a string into their own title field runs it on every later load.
remediation: Build list items with createElement and textContent (or one escape function applied at both sinks). Never put user or server text into innerHTML.

title: Titles of shared notes from the server are inserted as raw HTML
evidence: Traced app.js:44-46. The response of /api/shared is parsed as JSON and each s.title is interpolated into a template string that goes to insertAdjacentHTML('beforeend', ...). Nothing escapes it. The data comes from other users ("shared notes"), so it is not the viewer's own input.
failing_case: Another user shares a note titled ``. The viewer types any character in the search box. The server returns that note, the title is parsed as HTML, onerror runs in the page origin and sends every private note in localStorage away.
remediation: Build the <li> with document.createElement and textContent (or escape at one helper used for every title), and validate that the response is an array of objects with string titles before use.

title: Notes cannot be opened or deleted by keyboard: list rows and the delete control are not focusable, and delete is hover-only
evidence: Driven: pressing Tab 8 times from the page start visited search, New note, title, body, then left the page and wrapped; no list row or delete control ever took focus (tab_order in the run). Rows are plain li with a delegated click handler (app.js:30-33); the delete control is a div with an inline onclick (app.js:12) and styles.css:12 sets it to opacity 0 until :hover, so touch users cannot see it either. No names for screen readers.
failing_case: A keyboard-only or screen-reader user with two saved notes presses Tab: they can reach the editor for the first note only. They cannot switch to the second note and cannot delete any note. A touch user on a phone never sees the delete bin.
remediation: Render each row as a real button (or a link) for open, and a real <button aria-label="Delete note: TITLE"> for delete, always visible or shown on :focus-within as well as :hover. Keep the delegated handler but key it on those buttons.

title: Viewport meta blocks pinch zoom
evidence: index.html:5 sets maximum-scale=1 (WCAG 1.4.4 Resize text, AA).
failing_case: A low-vision user on a phone can not enlarge the 12 px hint or the note text on iOS/Android browsers that honour it.
remediation: Use content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1".

title: Title and body fields have no label or name; search uses a placeholder as its only label
evidence: index.html:13, 19, 20: no <label>, aria-label or placeholder on #title and #body; #search has only a placeholder.
failing_case: A screen reader announces 'edit text' and 'edit text multiline' with no purpose, so the user can not tell which field is the title (WCAG 1.3.1, 3.3.2, 4.1.2).
remediation: Add <label for> (visually hidden if the design needs) to #search, #title and #body.

title: Unguarded load: corrupt, wrong-shape or old-shape saved data kills the whole app
evidence: Driven. notes='{bad': JSON.parse throws, then 'notes is not defined' and 'Cannot access notes before initialization' in app.js; New note does nothing (0 rows). notes='{"a":1}': 'notes.filter is not a function'. Records without a title ([{id:1,body:'x'}]): "Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'toLowerCase')" at app.js:6 and an empty list. No version field on the saved shape.
failing_case: One bad write, a manual edit, or a record from an older version makes every page load throw. The page shows an empty list and dead controls. The next successful persist would overwrite the user's remaining data.
remediation: Wrap the parse in try/catch, validate that the result is an array of {id,title,body,updated} and coerce missing fields, keep the raw string under a backup key on failure, and save a schema version.

title: No flush on pagehide or unload: edits in the last 500 ms are lost
evidence: Traced the whole of store.js and app.js: the only write for edits is the 500 ms timeout. No pagehide, visibilitychange or beforeunload handler exists.
failing_case: Type a sentence into the body and refresh or close the tab within half a second. The timer never runs; on reload the sentence is gone, and the hint still said 'Changes save automatically'.
remediation: Add a pagehide/visibilitychange handler that runs the pending save synchronously, and make the save function callable without the timer.

title: The debounced save writes to whatever note is current when the timer fires; switching notes inside 500 ms discards the edit
evidence: Driven: two notes A and B; edited A's body to 'a edited', clicked B within 500 ms, waited 900 ms. localStorage afterwards: A.body still 'a0' (edit lost) and B.updated changed to the current time though B was never touched. Cause: store.js:16-18 read the inputs at fire time and write into the global currentNote, which openNote has already switched.
failing_case: Type a sentence into note A, then click note B within half a second. The sentence is gone from storage and from A when reopened; B gets a bogus 'updated' stamp that reorders the rank.
remediation: Capture the target note (and its values) when scheduling. Flush the pending save inside openNote before switching, and keep one writer per note.

title: First run and after delete: the editor accepts typing with no note selected, then the save timer throws and the text is silently lost
evidence: Driven with empty storage: filled #title, waited 800 ms. pageerror "Cannot set properties of null (setting 'title')", localStorage 'notes' still null, hint still reads 'Changes save automatically'. Second case driven: type into body, hover and delete the active note, timer fires: same TypeError (removeNote sets currentNote = null at app.js:26 while the save is pending). The UI shows no empty state or message; title and body stay enabled (index.html:19-20).
failing_case: A new user opens the page, sees an empty list and an enabled editor, types a note and sees 'Changes save automatically'. Nothing is stored. Same for a user who deletes the open note within 500 ms of typing.
remediation: Disable the editor and show 'No notes yet. Choose New note.' while currentNote is null; guard the timer callback against a null or deleted target.

title: Write failures are swallowed while the page keeps saying 'Changes save automatically'
evidence: Driven: replaced Storage.prototype.setItem with a function that throws, edited the body, waited. No error, no pageerror, hint text unchanged. persist() (store.js:23-27) returns nothing, so createNote, scheduleSave and deleteNote cannot know it failed. In private mode or on a full quota every write fails this way.
failing_case: Storage is full (many notes, or Safari private mode). The user writes for an hour, sees 'Changes save automatically', closes the tab. Everything since the last successful write is gone.
remediation: Have persist return success or the error, show a visible failure state ('Not saved: storage is full. Export your notes.') and change the hint to match the real state.

title: Fixed 1200 px container and 300 px sidebar column: the page scrolls sideways on a phone and at 200% zoom
evidence: Driven at 390 px wide: document scrollWidth 1222. The grid at styles.css:7 is fixed 300px 1fr with no media query anywhere in the file.
failing_case: On a 390 px phone the list and editor are cut off; the user must scroll horizontally to see the editor. Same at 200% zoom on a 1360 px laptop (reflow, WCAG 1.4.10).
remediation: Use max-width: 1200px with width: 100% and padding; switch .layout to a single column under about 700 px.

title: Focus outline removed with no replacement (WCAG 2.4.7)
evidence: Driven: focused #new and read computed outline-style: none. Inputs have a 1 px #eee border (styles.css:13) and the button has no focus style, so nothing changes visibly on focus.
failing_case: A keyboard user tabbing through search, New note, title and body cannot tell which control has focus.
remediation: Delete the rule, or replace it with a :focus-visible outline of at least 2 px in a colour with 3:1 contrast against the background.

title: Rank text and hint are light grey on white: about 1.9:1 and 1.6:1
evidence: Computed relative luminance: #bbb is 0.497 so 1.05/0.547 = 1.9:1 on #fff; #ccc (styles.css:15, .hint, 12 px) is 0.604 so 1.6:1. WCAG 1.4.3 needs 4.5:1. The input border #eee (styles.css:13) is about 1.2:1, below the 3:1 of 1.4.11.
failing_case: The "#3" rank and the "Changes save automatically" hint are close to unreadable for low-vision users or on a dim or sunlit screen. The input boxes have no visible edge.
remediation: Use at least #595959 for small text on white and #767676 or darker for input borders. Keep a token for each.

title: After deleting the open note the editor still shows it and further typing goes nowhere
evidence: Traced app.js:23-28. currentNote is set to null but the title and body inputs are not cleared or disabled. scheduleSave then dereferences null (store.js:16).
failing_case: Open a note, click its trash icon. The note's text stays in the editor. The user types more; after 500 ms a TypeError is thrown and nothing is saved, with no message. The user believes the text is saved.
remediation: Clear and disable the editor (or open a neighbour note) when the current note is deleted, and show the empty state.

title: Notes can only be opened by mouse click on a plain <li>
evidence: Traced app.js:10, 30-33. List items have no tabindex, role, key handler or button/link inside; selection is shown by a background colour only (styles.css:10) and no aria-current.
failing_case: A keyboard or screen-reader user presses Tab from 'New note': focus jumps to the title input. No note in the list can be reached or opened (WCAG 2.1.1, level A). The active note is signalled by colour alone (1.4.1).
remediation: Make each row contain a <button> (or link) that opens the note, with aria-current="true" on the active one.

title: Delete control is invisible until hover, so touch and focus users never see it
evidence: opacity is 0 and it appears only on :hover. There is no :focus-within rule and no touch alternative. Traced from the CSS.
failing_case: On a phone there is no hover, so the delete icon is invisible, yet a tap on that area still deletes (opacity does not disable the click). A keyboard user who got focus onto it would see nothing.
remediation: Show the control at rest at a reduced weight, and add `li:focus-within .del`; on touch devices always show it.

quote: const sorted = notes.slice().sort((a, b) => b.updated - a.updated);
title: renderList copies and sorts the full list once per row and rebuilds innerHTML with +=: about 1.3 s at 500 notes
evidence: Driven: 500 seeded notes, renderList('') took 1308 ms in Chromium. Per call the cost is O(n^2 log n) from the sort inside shown.forEach (app.js:8-9) plus n reparses of the growing list.innerHTML (app.js:10). renderList runs on every search keystroke (app.js:42) and every openNote (app.js:20).
failing_case: A user with 500 notes (10x of 50) waits over a second per keystroke in the search box and per note click.
remediation: Sort once before the loop, compute ranks in a Map, build the rows in a DocumentFragment (or one joined string) and assign once. Debounce search.

title: Delete is immediate and irreversible: no confirmation, no undo
evidence: app.js:23-28 removes the note and persists in one step; the delete control is a small icon revealed on hover (styles.css:12) sitting inside the row that opens the note. Driven: one click on the bin removed the note.
failing_case: User aims at a row, clicks the bin by mistake: the note and its body are gone from storage with no way back.
remediation: Keep deleted notes for a few seconds with an 'Undo' action in a live region, or ask 'Delete note TITLE?' before removing.

title: Clicking a shared-note row throws and leaves currentNote undefined
evidence: Driven: searched 'a' with a shared result, clicked li.shared. pageerror "Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'title')". The shared row has no data-id (app.js:46) so Number(undefined) is NaN, notes.find returns undefined and currentNote is set to undefined (app.js:17-18). Rows look clickable (cursor: pointer, styles.css:9).
failing_case: User searches, sees a shared note, clicks it: nothing opens, the console shows a TypeError, and the next keystroke in the editor throws again from the save timer.
remediation: Ignore rows without a data-id, or give shared rows a defined action (open read-only). Make openNote return early when the id is not found.

title: The list is never re-rendered after a save, so titles and the '#rank' badge go stale
evidence: Driven: renamed the open note 'A' to 'Renamed', waited 800 ms: list rows still read ['A','B']. scheduleSave (store.js:13-21) persists but does not call renderList, and the rank badge depends on 'updated'.
failing_case: User renames a note and the sidebar keeps the old name. Searching for the new name finds nothing until another action re-renders. The rank shown for a note that was just edited is wrong.
remediation: Re-render (or update the one row) after each save, via one function that owns state change then render.

title: Search responses are applied in arrival order, so a slow reply for an old query lands under the new query's list
evidence: Driven: typed 'ab' with the reply for 'a' delayed 600 ms and 'ab' immediate. Final shared rows: ['STALE-a', 'FRESH-ab']. The handler (app.js:40-48) has no abort, no sequence check, and appends with insertAdjacentHTML to whatever the list currently holds. res.ok is not checked either, so an error page is parsed as JSON. Every keystroke also sends the query to the server with no debounce.
failing_case: User types 'ab' on a slow link. Results for 'a' arrive after those for 'ab' and are shown as if they matched 'ab'. Clearing the box can also leave rows from an earlier query appended after the local list.
remediation: Debounce the input, use an AbortController (abort the previous request), check res.ok, and render local and shared rows from one state update keyed to the latest query.

quote: button { background: #6366f1; color: #fff; border: 0; padding: 8px 14px; border-radius: 8px; }
title: White text on #6366f1 (and on the hero's #8b5cf6 end) is under 4.5:1
evidence: Computed: #6366f1 luminance 0.185 gives 4.46:1 against white, and #8b5cf6 luminance 0.198 gives 4.23:1. The button text and the hero paragraph (styles.css:3, index.html:11) are normal-size text. WCAG 1.4.3.
failing_case: The "New note" label and the hero paragraph sit just under the AA threshold; the right side of the hero is the worst.
remediation: Darken the button to #4f46e5 or darker (about 6.3:1) and darken the gradient end.

title: Deleting a note re-renders without the active search filter
evidence: Driven: with notes A and B, typed 'B' in search (1 row), deleted that row: the list showed 1 row (A) while the search box still read 'B'.
failing_case: User filters, deletes a match, and sees unrelated notes listed under a filter that should exclude them.
remediation: Call renderList(document.getElementById('search').value), or keep the filter in one variable that renderList reads.

quote: const note = { id: Date.now(), title: 'Untitled', body: '', updated: Date.now() };
title: Date.now() ids collide; deleting one of two notes with the same id removes both
evidence: Driven: createNote() twice in one tick returned the same id (true); deleteNote(a.id) left 0 notes. deleteNote filters by id (store.js:30) and openNote finds the first match (app.js:17).
failing_case: Two notes created in the same millisecond (script, fast automation, a future import or sync) share an id: opening the second shows the first, and deleting either deletes both.
remediation: Use crypto.randomUUID() (or a counter persisted with the data) and migrate old numeric ids on load.

quote: Lorem ipsum dolor sit amet, your notes, supercharged.
title: Placeholder lorem ipsum and 'Welcome to' hero copy shipped in the page
evidence: index.html:11, rendered in the 60 px-padded hero at the top of every load. The hero pushes the real tool down by about 150 px.
failing_case: Every user sees 'Lorem ipsum dolor sit amet' as the product tagline.
remediation: Remove the hero or replace it with a one-line app title; no placeholder text.
